title: Bonds Fixing Failing & Aging Infrastructure; Improving Safety, Vocational Facilities
ballot_label: Bonds Fixing Failing & Aging Infrastructure; Improving Safety, Vocational Facilities. Shall District issue bonds to increase safety, security, repair aging schools and failing infrastructure, expand vocational classrooms, secure matching funds? If the bonds are approved, they will be payable from taxes on property or property ownership that are not subject to the limits of sections 11 and 11b, Article XI of the Oregon Constitution.
summary: Hillsboro School District No. 1J asks voters to approve $430 million in general obligation bonds for capital costs, including repairs to aging buildings and systems, safety and security upgrades, expanded career and technical education classrooms, and other projects. The ballot summary estimates a levy rate of $1.84 per $1,000 of assessed value, says the district would be eligible for $6.1 million in state matching funds, and requires a community oversight committee and regular audits.
yes_means: A yes vote approves the district issuing $430 million in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes outside the constitutional limits, for school repairs, safety and security, and vocational facilities.
no_means: A no vote rejects the district issuing these general obligation bonds and the associated property tax.
fiscal_impact: Per the ballot summary: principal amount $430 million; estimated levy rate $1.84 per $1,000 of assessed value; bonds may be issued in multiple series, each maturing within 21 years; district eligible for $6.1 million in state matching funds if passed.
gaps: No YES arguments collected: the county voters' pamphlet measure pages (WC-59 to WC-65) could not be read, and no attributed statement from a YES committee or supporter was found in searches.
No NO arguments collected: the county voters' pamphlet measure pages could not be read, and no attributed opposition statement was found in searches.

collection_notes: Oregon local ballot titles have no official result-of-vote text; yes_means/no_means are neutral one-sentence descriptions written by the collector strictly from the official ballot caption/question. Ballot caption, question and summary facts were taken from the Multnomah County sample ballot for Nov 3, 2026 (multco.us, T1), because the Washington County ballot-title PDF is a scanned image; the caption matches the Washington County current-election listing and inventory.json exactly. The ballot_label was assembled from consecutive verbatim quotes returned by WebFetch (the tool caps single quotes), so a verifier should confirm it against the PDF. Jurisdiction and number match the inventory; multco.us lists the filing date as 8/27/2026. District pages say the board voted unanimously on May 26, 2026 to refer the bond. Per-side T3 searches found no attributed YES or NO statements; KPTV (May 28, 2026, FOX 12 Staff) reports only district figures. The Washington County Nov 3, 2026 voters' pamphlet lists this measure in its table of contents, but the fetchable text layer of the PDF ends at about page WC-29 (119,746 characters), so the measure pages (ballot title, explanatory statement, arguments) could not be read. The county ballot-title PDF linked from the current-election page is a scanned image with no machine-readable text. A verifier or human with a PDF/OCR viewer should check the pamphlet measure pages for filed arguments. The session-wide WebSearch budget ran out before the final per-side '"Measure <number>" <jurisdiction>' search could be run; the allowed_domains T3 search was rejected by the search proxy (HTTP 400) on every attempt, so T3 coverage relies on plain searches. Outlet-specific follow-up searches were not possible.
